overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by not naming the individual appointment candidates on the Sept. 27 notice; no deliberation violation was found, earlier complaints were untimely, and non-OML claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Sept. 27 meeting notice listed only 'Appointments for Town Boards/Committees' without naming the individuals the Board would consider for appointment, reappointment, or removal.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the notice for the Board’s September 27 meeting should have included the names of the individuals to be considered by the Board.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board deliberated on the appointments outside a posted meeting before the Sept. 27 meeting, including a conversation between two members.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law, as we find no evidence of deliberation outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Five earlier complaints about notices for June through September meetings were filed more than 30 days after the alleged violations, so they were untimely.
allegations.key_passage: As only the allegation regarding sufficiency of the notice for the September 27 meeting is timely, we decline to review the other five complaints.

allegations.summary: Allegations that the Board failed to interview potential candidates and violated town policies were not claims under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. Accordingly, we decline to review them.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
No further relief: the Board's November 15 re-vote on the Agricultural and Conservation Commissions already reinstated the affected members
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. As the Board re-voted at the November 15 meeting on the composition of the Agricultural Commission and Conservation Commission, in order to reinstate Mr. Clark and Ms. Cook-Obregon, we order no further relief.
